item.title: Five arrested in major drug trafficking operation
item.description: Five people, four men and a woman, were arrested in a drug trafficking operation across Żejtun, Ħal Tarxien, Raħal Ġdid, il-Fgura, Birkirkara and Ħaż-Żebbuġ, together with a further arrest in Marsaxlokk. Interior Minister Glenn Bedingfield said the seized items included cocaine, crack cocaine and heroin, about €8,000 in cash, luxury vehicles, phones, SIM cards, electronic equipment, weapons, documents and business stock.

item.title: Abela says EU budget financing and fairness still need work after revised plan
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela said further work is needed on how the EU's 2028-2034 long-term budget is financed after an extraordinary European Council session on the multi-annual financial framework. He said the revised proposal tabled by Council President António Costa addressed a number of Malta's concerns, but that a balance and fair outcome still have to be struck. Before the summit, Abela joined the 17-member Friends of Cohesion group, which reaffirmed that Cohesion Policy must remain central to the EU's future budget. No agreement was reached.

item.title: SDM secures first-ever majority at MCAST student council
item.description: Student organisation SDM won seven of the 13 seats on MCAST's student council, with 6,694 votes, in the first time it has secured a majority at the institution. Five seats went to independent candidates with 4,533 votes and Pulse took one with 2,429. The result follows SDM's sweep of the Junior College student council a week earlier.

item.title: Judge asks to see Ricky Caruana's PBS contract as PN impartiality case continues
item.description: The judge in the Nationalist Party's impartiality case against PBS and the Broadcasting Authority asked to see presenter Ricky Caruana's contract with the public broadcaster before allowing questions about his social media posts. Separately, the Broadcasting Authority told the court it took no further action against PBS over earlier impartiality rulings, with the PBS CEO saying privately contracted presenters are not questioned about their political ties.

item.title: Government launches Malta's second National AI Strategy with 86 measures for 2026-2030
item.description: Economy Minister Silvio Schembri unveiled the strategy while opening the TECHXPO technology exhibition, saying it sets out 86 measures for 2026-2030 aimed at citizens, businesses, public institutions and researchers, and underpins the Malta Vision 2050 goals. He said around 80% of the actions under the first AI strategy had already been implemented, and that the new document places public trust at the centre of how Malta develops and uses artificial intelligence. The strategy was drawn up after a consultation involving more than 25 experts, over 70 individual stakeholders and feedback from more than 100 entities, with over 350 people taking part in seven public consultations, and it also covers widening access to AI training and computing infrastructure.

item.title: Enemalta lays six kilometres of new cables to reinforce Birkirkara's electricity network
item.description: Enemalta has installed around six kilometres of new 11kV cables across Birkirkara, replacing sections prone to faults and adding roughly 600 metres of low-voltage feeders. Energy Minister Miriam Dalli, who visited the site with Enemalta and Birkirkara council representatives, said the works address current demand while anticipating future needs. The project forms part of the company's nine-year plan to reinforce, renew and expand the distribution network across Malta and Gozo, covering cables, feeders, substations and distribution centres.

item.title: PN demands urgent talks after hotel licence fee and eco-contribution hikes
item.description: The Nationalist Party said the budget's higher hotel licence fees and tourism eco-contribution increases were announced without proper consultation with operators, calling for urgent talks with sector associations. The Malta Hotels and Restaurants Association separately warned that rising licence fees, increased eco-contributions and the cost of employing third-country nationals risk undermining Malta's tourism competitiveness.

item.title: Gozo Tourism Association proposes flat €4 eco-contribution for all accommodation
item.description: The GTA wants a flat €4 per person per night levy across all tourist accommodation in Gozo, a six-month postponement of the new rates until 1 July 2027, and a cap at seven nights per stay. It says the budget's increase of the eco-contribution from €1.50 to €8 per night for hotels and €10 for short lets, from 1 January, has already triggered booking cancellations for 2027.

item.title: Documentary 'Dear Decision Makers' brings hidden stories behind Malta's abortion laws to the screen
item.description: A new documentary by the grassroots campaign Dear Decision Makers explores pregnancy, abortion and reproductive healthcare in Malta through anonymous testimonies, animation and interviews with activists. Co-directed by Rosie Litterick and Sandie Von Brockdorff, the film builds on the campaign's collection of testimonies since 2021 and aims to put real lives behind the ongoing political debate.

item.title: Nurses say foreign staff are being recruited out of Malta to Australia, Ireland and the UK
item.description: Nurses union representatives said Maltese nurses are being headhunted to work in Australia, Ireland and England, worsening staff shortages in the local health service. Union officials highlighted the closure of hospital wards, the influx of third-country nationals and growing pressure on staff as the main changes in recent years, and said the unions have expanded their role in protecting workers.

item.title: Two hunters caught using illegal electronic bird callers in Mellieħa
item.description: Police intervened after the Malta Rangers Unit reported the use of electronic bird callers near the White Tower in Armier, inside a Natura 2000 protected site. The rangers said one hunter fired five consecutive shots when the maximum is three, and that the callers were found after he swam out to retrieve ducks. The unit says the area is becoming a hotspot for illegal hunting.

item.title: Joseph Muscat says MEP elections took priority over Clyde Caruana's population report
item.description: Former prime minister Joseph Muscat acknowledged that the controversial 2018 population report was discussed within his administration but said European Parliament elections and other priorities took precedence. He estimated the document was around 800 pages, which differs from Clyde Caruana's earlier description of it as nearly 300 pages long, and said the foreign workers issue was no longer the key concern.

item.title: Nine people with disabilities complete programmes for independent living and employment
item.description: Six participants completed Aġenzija Sapport's 25-week Way to Work programme and three completed Skills4Life, covering job readiness, workplace behaviour, personal care and money management, along with workplace visits and volunteering. item.title: Repeat offender caught gambling at casino during court-imposed curfew
item.description: Adrian Muscat, 43, a contractor from Żurrieq, was arrested after police received information that he had been seen gambling at a casino in Portomaso using another person's ID card, while he should have been observing his curfew. CCTV footage showed him gambling, and he pleaded guilty to breaching bail conditions and using a false identity. He is already facing money laundering and theft proceedings over three luxury vehicles taken from a St Julian's hotel.

item.title: Government deficit nearly doubles to €695 million as debt passes €12 billion
item.description: Malta's Consolidated Fund deficit stood at €695.4 million at the end of October, up €321.5 million (about 86%) from €373.9 million a year earlier, as spending grew faster than revenue. Recurrent revenue rose to €7,129.2 million, led by income tax, VAT and social security contributions, while total expenditure climbed €1,069.3 million to €7,824.5 million, with social security benefits, energy support measures and medicines among the largest increases. Central Government debt reached €12,182.7 million, almost €1 billion more than a year earlier.

item.title: Planning Authority approves 122-unit block in Żurrieq's contested Nigret area
item.description: The Planning Authority approved the 122-unit Block D development in Żurrieq's Nigret area by six votes to one, with environmental NGO representative Romano Cassar casting the sole vote against. The project by Best Deal Zurrieq Ltd comprises 23 maisonettes, 78 apartments and 21 penthouses, with 276 garages and parking for 336 cars, plus landscaped public open space. The approval follows a separate permit for a 68-unit Block B1 on the same site, awarded on 23 November.

item.title: Tourism Minister declines to comment on calls to postpone eco-tax hike
item.description: Tourism Minister Jo Etienne Abela refused to comment on growing industry concerns about the 2027 Budget eco-contribution increase, saying the government line stands and discussions are ongoing. From 1 January the tourist accommodation eco-contribution rises from €1.50 to €8 per night for hotels (capped at €64) and to €10 per night for short lets (capped at €80). The Malta Hotels and Restaurants Association and the Gozo Tourism Association are lobbying to postpone the hike.

item.title: Minister Camilleri puts mental health and wellbeing at the heart of education
item.description: Education Minister Byron Camilleri said education can only succeed if mental health and wellbeing sit at the centre of everything done for students and educators, speaking at the second edition of the national EduVoices conference. The event, themed 'Your Voice. Your Wellbeing. Our Future', brought together students, educators, parents and experts including representatives from UNESCO and the OECD.

item.title: Contractor delays held up Triq tal-Qares repaving, Enemalta says
item.description: Enemalta said reinstatement works on a section of Triq tal-Qares in Mosta will begin in the coming days after delays by the private contractor engaged for them. Parts of the road were left with a concrete surface following underground works carried out by Enemalta in August 2026. The paving will be restored to its original state once the works are completed.

item.title: Business activity remains below historic average, Central Bank says
item.description: The Central Bank of Malta said economic conditions were broadly unchanged in October compared with September, with business activity still below its long-term average. The bank's Business Conditions Index showed industrial production and retail trade accelerating while growth in tourism expenditure slowed, and consumer sentiment declined but remained strong by historical standards.

item.title: KM Malta Airlines and Air India sign codeshare deal from 1 December
item.description: KM Malta Airlines and Air India will launch a codeshare agreement on 1 December, allowing passengers to book journeys between India and Malta on a single ticket. Air India will place its code on selected KM Malta Airlines flights from Malta to Amsterdam, Paris, Rome, London Gatwick, London Heathrow and Zurich, with baggage checked through. The deal builds on an existing interline partnership and does not introduce direct Malta-India flights.

item.title: €3.4 million in payments to 882 people under 2026 anomalies scheme
item.description: A total of 882 people, or their heirs, will receive €3.4 million in compensation payments under the government's 2026 anomalies scheme, Social Policy and Family Minister Michael Falzon said. Two additional schemes were introduced to address past employment injustices affecting former workers of International Aeradio Ltd and the Rediffusion Group of Companies, whose pension-related benefit claims were previously rejected by the courts.

item.title: Mother appeals jail term over son's use of her passport in illegal migration scheme
item.description: A pregnant mother with seven children appealed a three-month prison sentence for helping a relative enter Malta illegally using someone else's passport, arguing the court did not consider the children dependent on her care. She and her eldest son admitted transferring passport details to help a cousin's wife enter Malta without documentation; the cousin was also jailed for three months.

item.title: Gozo tourism body objects to higher accommodation licence fees
item.description: The Gozo Tourism Association has objected to the higher accommodation licence fees announced in the 2027 Budget, adding to calls from tourism lobby groups for the eco-contribution increase to be deferred. The association has proposed a flat €4 eco-contribution for all accommodation and warned of cancellations in 2027 if the current terms stand.

item.title: Motorcyclist grievously injured in Mġarr crash
item.description: A 30-year-old man residing in San Ġwann was grievously injured after losing control of his Znen motorcycle in Triq l-Imġarr, Mġarr, at about 9:15pm on Thursday. Police were informed and a medical team transported the rider to Mater Dei Hospital, where he was later certified to be suffering from grievous injuries. Police investigations are ongoing.
